The client arrived ready to work and the behavior technician began the session without difficulty.

The behavior technician ran Discrete Trial Training (DTT) on the money identification program using a three-item array of one, five and ten dollar denominations. Prompting started at full physical and the technician faded to a gestural prompt by the sixth trial, after the client began orienting to the correct bill before the prompt was delivered. The client responded correctly on eight of twelve trials, and the final four of those were independent. During snack the technician moved to Natural Environment Teaching (NET), targeting requesting on the client's Augmentative and Alternative Communication (AAC) device, and the client produced five unprompted mands across the period. The tacting colors program did not run today; the session ran out of time before the technician reached it.

Before each demand the behavior technician presented a first-then board, and the client chose the reinforcer up front rather than having one assigned. The technician gave a two-minute warning ahead of the move to table work and set a visual timer where the client could see it. Refusals dropped noticeably against the previous session, and the timer was the change the technician had made.

The client eloped from the table twice, both times during the money program. On each occasion the behavior technician blocked the elopement and redirected the client back with a gestural prompt. No self-injurious behavior occurred. The client protested loudly once during the transition; the technician did not attend to it, and the protest stopped after roughly twenty seconds.

The caregiver joined at the end of the session and asked the behavior technician how the AAC device should be used at home.
